name: The Railway Children
label: Factory Records
lede: Four Wigan teenagers made a Factory record, topped the indie chart, signed to Virgin and had an American radio No. 1. Then EMI bought Virgin.

eras.title: Wigan, not Manchester
eras.text: The Railway Children came out of Wigan, twenty miles west of the Haçienda, and were still teenagers when Factory took them on. They rehearsed in the same building as the Happy Mondays and played the pub-and-club circuit between the two towns.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Railway Children (band) · Wigan Today
years.h: Gary Newby starts the Railway Children in Wigan
years.p: [[Gary Newby|d29a33a4-c3cc-46b4-abaa-88d96e5de11f]] writes and sings, Brian Bateman plays rhythm guitar, Stephen Hull bass and Guy Keegan drums. Wigan Today says they shared a practice room with the [[Happy Mondays|01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf]].

years.h: Factory puts out A Gentle Sound as FAC 162
years.p: The band's first single, on [[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]]'s label while the members were still teenagers, AllMusic notes.

eras.title: An indie No. 1 and a major on the phone
eras.text: One year on Factory: a second single and a debut album that both went to the top of the UK indie chart. The album was the record that got Virgin interested.

years.h: Brighter, FAC 167, goes to No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: The second Factory single, per Wigan Today. It turns up again as a track on the debut album.

years.cap: The Railway Children, the original four, c. 1987
years.h: Reunion Wilderness tops the UK indie albums chart
years.p: Recorded at Revolution Studios with producers Mike Johnson and Nick Garside. NME gives it 9 out of 10.
years.xp:
Toppermost hears it as the band's starkest record, "bold, stark and metallic" next to the polish that came later. Trouser Press was cooler, crediting Newby's voice and calling the ringing guitars and brisk acoustics routine.

The CD had two extra songs, "A Gentle Sound" and "Content", that weren't on the vinyl.

years.h: Virgin Records signs the band off the back of the album
years.p: AllMusic says Reunion Wilderness led straight to a Virgin contract. The Railway Children leave Factory after two singles and one LP.

eras.title: Virgin, R.E.M. and American radio
eras.text: On Virgin the guitars got shinier and the songs got bigger. Tours with R.E.M. and the Sugarcubes came first; then a single that went to No. 1 on American modern rock radio and, on its second try, into the UK Top 30.

years.h: Recurrence is the first Virgin album
years.p: Chiming guitars and steadier songwriting, as Toppermost puts it. It reaches No. 96 in the UK.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Railway Children (band) · Wigan Today
years.h: Support slots with R.E.M. in Europe and the Sugarcubes in the US
years.p: Two tours with bigger bands in one year, according to Wikipedia. Wigan Today adds [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] to the list of acts they toured with.

years.src: Wikipedia: Every Beat of the Heart
years.h: "Every Beat of the Heart" stalls at No. 68 in the UK
years.p: Newby's song, produced by Steve Lovell and Steve Power and mixed at Strawberry Studios in Stockport, goes out as the lead single. America takes longer to notice.

years.h: Four months in London studios for Native Place
years.p: Lovell and Power produce at the Townhouse and Battery. All 12 songs are Newby's; the album reaches No. 59 in the UK.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Newby found the long sessions frustrating. Matt Irving plays keyboards and accordion, Matthew Taylor saxophone.

Reviews mostly liked it: MusicHound Rock called it one of the definitive pop albums of the early '90s. Trouser Press thought the band had gone too far toward the dancefloor.

years.h: MTV's 120 Minutes has the band in to talk with Dave Kendall
years.p: The band stop by MTV's alternative show to talk about Native Place, the year the video went into rotation.

years.src: Wikipedia: Every Beat of the Heart
years.h: "Every Beat of the Heart" is No. 1 on Billboard Modern Rock
years.p: The video premiered on MTV in July. By September the song had topped Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart.

years.src: Wikipedia: Every Beat of the Heart · Wikipedia: Native Place · Toppermost
yt: Every Beat of the Heart on Top of the Pops
years.h: Virgin reissues "Every Beat of the Heart" and it reaches No. 24
years.p: Second time round the song hits No. 24 in the UK on February 17 and No. 28 in Ireland, and the band play Top of the Pops.
years.xp: The band toured Native Place with the Heart Throbs, and turned up on kids' TV too: BBC's Going Live! and ITV's Motormouth, per Toppermost.

eras.title: EMI buys Virgin
eras.text: The fourth album was in progress when EMI bought Virgin, and the Railway Children left the label. Newby carried the name on his own for two more records and a working life in Japan.

years.h: EMI takes over Virgin, and the Railway Children part ways with it
years.p: AllMusic says the band were working on Dream Arcade at the time. Native Place's Wikipedia page counts the takeover among the reasons the band came apart.

years.h: Bateman and Hull leave; Keegan goes to the Tansads
years.p: By 1994 AllMusic has Bateman and Hull gone. Keegan drums for The Tansads, the Crash Band and the Ultras.

years.h: Newby finishes Dream Arcade with session players
years.p: The album started under Virgin comes out on Ether Records with Newby the only original member on it.

years.h: Newby moves into writing and arranging for Japanese artists
years.p: From 2002 Wikipedia has him working in Japan, writing and arranging for other people.

years.h: Gentle Sound on Ether
years.p: Another Railway Children album from Newby, its title borrowed from the 1986 Factory debut single.

eras.title: Four men in a Standish pub
eras.text: Twenty-three years after they last played together, the original four met in a pub in Standish and found they still knew the songs. The reunion ran three years, starting in Brooklyn and ending in London.

q: It all just came flowing back.
years.h: The original four meet at the Boar's Head in Standish
years.p: Bateman hadn't played guitar in about 20 years, Wigan Today reported. The first rehearsal went fine anyway.
years.xp: Keegan told Wigan Today that once they were in the room, "it all just came flowing back." Hull and Bateman had left music altogether after the split.

years.cap: The Railway Children at NYC Popfest, Brooklyn, May 2016
years.src: Wigan Today · Wikipedia: The Railway Children (band)
yt: Brighter, live at Shiiine On Weekender 2016
years.h: First show back is in Brooklyn, at NYC Popfest
years.p: Then the Ruby Lounge in Manchester and Shiiine On Weekender at Butlin's in Minehead, where they played "Brighter".

years.cap: The Railway Children at the Borderline, London, May 2018
years.h: Last show at the Borderline in London
years.p: The reunion ends in a small Soho club. Wikipedia lists it as the band's final concert.
